effect_mechanism: Water harvesting buffers dry periods by storing or infiltrating water: zai pits reduce the impact of dry spells of a few weeks when soil water storage is sufficient, runoff ponds in semi-arid Brazil supply supplemental irrigation and production cisterns supply livestock water, cisterns in China are reported to mitigate frequent droughts, and public-works interventions in Ethiopia raised water availability. WOCAT compilers for Vallerani micro-catchments, ponds, check dams, terraces, stone lines and water-spreading weirs judge drought impacts reduced through stored water, infiltration and soil moisture retention, and households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought. In a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1].
conditionality: Much of the pool is practitioner judgement from technology sheets or expert assertion (Brazilian research and programme authors, a lender evaluation in China without measurement), and only the Rwanda unit, reported second-hand in a completion report, and the Kenyan sand-dam catchment table, whose values are likely interview-derived, rest on comparisons against controls [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. The Ethiopian study notes vegetation greenness still tracked local drought severity, the Haiti compiler states the impact is not yet measured, and the zai effect depends on soil storage capacity. Storage itself runs short in prolonged drought: subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry out in a rainless year, and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limited soil-conservation benefits; these units record no benefit at that point, a shortfall rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

effect_mechanism: Terraces, contour stone bunds and lines, check dams, sand dams and water-spreading structures slow and spread runoff and retain water and sediment, lowering peak discharges and lengthening flood rise times; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50%, and WOCAT compilers for many of these structures judge downstream flooding reduced. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive fewer rainy-season floods, and spate and diversion structures in Yemen are said to control floods. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage in the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1].
conditionality: Most units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and catchment-scale measurement is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Yemen and Uttarakhand statements are lender self-reported. Direction depends on design: diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes raised peak flows, larger sand dams increase flooding risk, a conservation-tillage sheet from the Philippines rated flood impacts worse, and a farm pond in India was rated neutral. The same review finds check dams have a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where ill-designed or poorly maintained; its positive cases are secondary citations, and the Italian ones are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2].

effect_mechanism: Water harvesting and conservation structures capture runoff and raise soil moisture so rainfed crops yield more, especially in dry years and low-rainfall areas; stored water allows supplemental irrigation and extra crops, and sediment and organic matter trapped behind structures add fertility. Meta-analyses now carry much of the evidence: A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a pooled yield gain of 71% over controls, with 142% for infiltration pits, 91% for mulching, 69% for soil and stone bunds, 48% for terraces and 74% for tied ridging [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_1, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_2, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_3, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_4, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_5, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_6]; a synthesis of Ethiopian studies gives mean grain-yield differences of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds, 554.3 for tied ridges, 629.2 for mulching and 108.4 for minimum tillage [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4, ev_crop_yield_adim16_5]; a sub-Saharan conservation agriculture meta-analysis finds yields 3.7% above conventional tillage overall, 8.4% for maize when all three principles are applied and 12.5% at sites with under 400 mm of seasonal rainfall, with the gain growing slowly over time [ev_crop_yield_corb20_1, ev_crop_yield_corb20_4, ev_crop_yield_corb20_6, ev_crop_yield_corb20_10]; and a terracing meta-analysis finds biomass on terraces about 1.94 times that on slopes, and reviewed studies report terraced teff, barley and maize yields at least two times those on slopes and 20% gains on young bench terraces in Peru [ev_crop_yield_wei16_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_2, ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]. In Burkina Faso stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% and by about 142% with compost, on-farm trials in Mozambique gave maize gains of 504 to 800 kg per hectare on planting basins and direct-seeded plots, in Malawi's El Niño season reduced tillage raised maize from 247 to 505 kg per hectare, and silt farmland behind check dams on China's Loess Plateau yields 6–10 times more than sloping farmland [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_3, ev_crop_yield_boil19_1, ev_crop_yield_luca21_1]. Stored water stabilises output: Indian farmers reported crop-failure chances falling from 20% to 6% in the rainy season and from 100% to 5–10% in winter with a farm pond, sand dams cut crop failure against a control catchment in Kenya, and WOCAT compilers across many technology sheets judge crop, fodder and animal production increased [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_2, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1].
conditionality: In the Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively (probably waterlogging), and stone bunds in semi-arid Tanzania reduced maize yield by 13% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6, ev_crop_yield_adim16_9]. Conservation agriculture meta-analyses add caveats: a global no-till meta-analysis finds yields 5.1% lower overall, 15.1% lower in tropical latitudes and 7.6% lower for maize, matching conventional tillage only under rainfed conditions in dry climates [ev_crop_yield_pitt15_1, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_2, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_3, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_4]; the sub-Saharan conservation agriculture meta-analysis finds yields 4.3% lower at sites with over 1,200 mm of seasonal rainfall, no significant gain for crops other than maize or for reduced tillage alone, and gains only with no-tillage rather than planting basins or minimum tillage [ev_crop_yield_corb20_7, ev_crop_yield_corb20_3, ev_crop_yield_corb20_5, ev_crop_yield_corb20_9]; and a maize meta-regression finds conservation agriculture consistently underperforms on high-clay soils in very wet seasons, though at median rainfall and clay it outperforms conventional practice even without fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_stew18_3, ev_crop_yield_stew18_4]; earlier meta-analyses also report losses in humid climates and where mean annual precipitation exceeds 1,000 mm, and in drought seasons in Mozambique and Zimbabwe conservation agriculture gave no harvest or yielded less than conventional tillage [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3, ev_crop_yield_knapp18_3, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_1, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7]. In Algeria farmers lost 5 to 15% of their cropped area to banquettes without seeing yields improve, legume yields between banquettes showed no significant gain, and a Moroccan farmer saw no yield improvement between banquettes imposed by technicians [ev_crop_yield_arab04_1, ev_crop_yield_arab04_2, ev_crop_yield_roos10_2]. Other nulls and negatives: conservation promoted mostly off-farm had no yield effect, benefits in Ethiopia appeared only once structures were maintained for at least seven years, zai lowered sorghum yields under waterlogging in Cameroon, diversion banquettes in Niger cut yields, and soil salinisation can appear on check-dam farmland [ev_crop_yield_luca21_1]. Outside the meta-analyses the pool mixes independent evaluations with lender completion-report figures, bundled watershed programmes, reviews quoting ranges from earlier studies, a farmer survey reported in a preprint and many practitioner judgements; much of the zai and planting-basin gain rides on added manure, compost or fertiliser [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1].

effect_mechanism: Soil and water conservation structures (terraces, bunds, check dams) retain moisture and soil, raising crop yields and value of production; the gains are larger in low-rainfall or climatically variable areas and in dry periods. effect_mechanism: Planting pits (zai, tassa), tied ridges and furrows, mulch, basin tillage and infiltration trenches capture runoff near the plants; combined with manure they let cereals be grown on degraded crusted soils, and in the 1990 drought in Niger only tassa fields produced a harvest. Meta-analyses quantify the gain: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds yield increases of 142% for infiltration pits, 91% for mulching and 74% for tied ridging over controls [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_2, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_3, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_6]; a synthesis of Ethiopian studies gives mean grain-yield differences of 554.3 kg per hectare for tied ridges, 629.2 for mulching and 108.4 for minimum tillage [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4, ev_crop_yield_adim16_5]; a sub-Saharan conservation agriculture meta-analysis finds yields 3.7% above conventional tillage overall, 8.4% for maize when all three principles are applied and 12.5% at sites with under 400 mm of seasonal rainfall, with the gain growing slowly over time [ev_crop_yield_corb20_1, ev_crop_yield_corb20_4, ev_crop_yield_corb20_6, ev_crop_yield_corb20_10]; a maize meta-regression finds conservation agriculture outperforms conventional practice at median rainfall and clay even without fertiliser and gains more as seasons get drier [ev_crop_yield_stew18_4, ev_crop_yield_stew18_1]; and earlier meta-analyses find no-till with residue retention and rotation raises rainfed yields by 7.3% in dry climates [ev_crop_yield_pittel15_2]. On farms, reduced tillage raised maize from 247 to 505 kg per hectare in Malawi's El Niño season and from 561.85 to 1273.52 kg per hectare in a good Kenyan season, first-year planting-basin farmers in Zimbabwe obtained 1520 kg against 368 kg per hectare, tied ridges raised maize significantly in Tanzania, review ranges for zai and tassa pits run to 100–200% yield gains, and planting basins and direct seeding in Mozambique gave maize gains of 504 to 800 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_boil19_1, ev_crop_yield_boil19_4, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_6, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_3]; WOCAT compilers for pits, contour bunds and conservation tillage in several countries judge crop production increased.
conditionality: A global no-till meta-analysis finds yields 5.1% lower overall, 15.1% lower in tropical latitudes and 7.6% lower for maize, matching conventional tillage only under rainfed conditions in dry climates [ev_crop_yield_pitt15_1, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_2, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_3, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_4]; the sub-Saharan conservation agriculture meta-analysis finds yields 4.3% lower at sites with over 1,200 mm of seasonal rainfall, no significant gain for crops other than maize or for reduced tillage alone, and gains only with no-tillage rather than planting basins or minimum tillage [ev_crop_yield_corb20_7, ev_crop_yield_corb20_3, ev_crop_yield_corb20_5, ev_crop_yield_corb20_9]; and a maize meta-regression finds conservation agriculture consistently underperforms on high-clay soils in very wet seasons [ev_crop_yield_stew18_3]. Earlier meta-analyses add that no-till lowers yields by 5.7% overall, yields fall under conservation agriculture where mean annual precipitation exceeds 1,000 mm, and yield stability is no better than under conventional tillage (a stability meta-analysis drawn mostly from high-income trials) [ev_crop_yield_pittel15_1, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3, ev_crop_yield_knapp18_1]. In drought seasons gains vanish: conservation agriculture pillars had no detectable effect in a Kenyan season with a failed start, tied ridging gave no advantage in Kenyan short rains with meteorological droughts, and in Mozambique and Zimbabwe conservation agriculture gave no harvest or yielded less than conventional tillage [ev_crop_yield_boil19_3, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_1, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7]. Much of the pit gain depends on manure or fertiliser (pits alone gave an average sorghum gain of only 38 kg/ha in one study against 310 kg/ha in another), zai lowered sorghum yields under waterlogging in Cameroon, the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, and the review ranges for pits are not pooled estimates [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_1].

effect_mechanism: Semi-circular bunds, Vallerani micro-catchments and trenches harvest runoff for crops and grasses: WOCAT compilers report crop production and biomass augmented several times over traditional techniques with the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso, higher millet and straw yields from cropland bunds on abandoned farmland in Niger, and more fodder and grazing days. Negarim micro-catchments with supplementary irrigation supported fruit production at Embrapa Semi-Arid in Brazil, and semi-circular bunds raised millet grain production under African conditions. A review tabulates crop yield increases of 50–200% from half-moons in Burkina Faso and Niger, and cites micro-basin water harvesting in Zambia doubling maize yields to 3 t per hectare [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_5].
conditionality: Apart from an FAO manual citing earlier work and a review quoting ranges from earlier studies, all units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, not measurements. Animal production was rated lower for trenches and semi-circular bunds in Niger because treated rangeland must be protected from grazing for the first years while vegetation establishes. The review figures are ranges and single citations rather than pooled estimates [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_5].

effect_mechanism: Terraces, fanya juu and contour stone bunds or lines level slopes and slow runoff so more water and soil stay on the field; yields of maize, barley, millet and sorghum rose on terraced or bunded land, especially in dry years. Stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% in Burkina Faso and by about 142% with compost, and millet yields in Niger rose by more than 40% up to 15 years after the bunds were built [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. effect_mechanism: Higher and more stable yields, irrigation of gardens and higher-value crops from stored water, and better fodder and livestock raise household income and food security; beneficiaries shift from staples to vegetables, and a quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_economic_return_mala24_1]. WOCAT compilers describe the same pathway: planting pits in Uganda keep banana stands fruiting through drought and raise harvests for sale, ripper tillage in Zambia gives better tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost, farm ponds in Cambodia supply irrigation during drought, and contour stone bunds in Bhutan enlarge the cultivable area for diverse crops [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1139_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. WOCAT compilers' own benefit-versus-cost ratings point the same way, judging the long-term returns on both establishment and maintenance positive or very positive on nearly every sheet. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. An Ethiopian synthesis reports positive net present values of 3486.2 Birr per hectare for stone bunds, 2794.0 for bench terraces and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3]; In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 USD per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots in the low-rainfall budget, with 866.84 against 357.16 for experienced farmers in high rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]; and ground cover raised the odds of a Malawian plot meeting the household maize requirement in the El Niño season, and planting basins sharply raised those odds in a good Kenyan season [ev_food_security_boil19_1, ev_food_security_boil19_2]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income and food security in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios of up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. Modelled bench-terrace gains in Peru could raise per capita incomes by up to 15%, and a review tabulates significantly increased food security and incomes from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi [ev_household_income_wei16_1, ev_food_security_ngur26_1].
conditionality: Most pooled units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT technology sheets, including compilers' benefit-versus-cost judgements rather than measured returns, and much of the literature comes from bundled watershed programmes and lender completion or appraisal reports, so measured household effects are a minority. Independent evaluations are more cautious: no significant effect on food security or total income in Ethiopian programmes, terraces reducing net crop income, a Brazilian production-cistern programme with a benefit-cost ratio far below break-even, single SWC measures not covering their annual costs, and sand dams likely not cost-efficient [ev_food_security_abate21_4, ev_food_security_arega24_1, ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_economic_return_zoug14_3, ev_economic_return_ritc21_1]. Compilers also rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and record no change on several sheets, including a subsistence farm pond in India; Kenyan sand dams sit inside a wider food-security programme, and food security, income and returns are all proxies for poverty [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Short-term returns on establishment are rated slightly to very negative on sheets from Tunisia, China, Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde, Nicaragua, Jordan, Uzbekistan and Somalia, reflecting up-front costs that are only recovered over time. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. New evidence adds further limits: the same synthesis reports negative net present values for graded fanya juu (−148 Birr per hectare) and graded soil bunds (−708 Birr per hectare), possibly because off-site benefits were left out [ev_economic_return_adim16_4]; cost savings from conservation agriculture are usually small for smallholders; and in a Kenyan drought season net benefits were higher without tied ridging [ev_economic_return_corb20_1, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]. The Zimbabwe planting-basin margins include manure and fertiliser and the high-rainfall figure is a sensitivity scenario, the Indian pond returns are cross-sectional from a preprint survey confounded by farm size and assets, the reviewed income and water-value figures are secondary citations at their upper end, and the Peruvian income gain is modelled [ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_household_income_wei16_1].

effect_mechanism: Zai pits, planting pits, contour bunds and reduced or ripper tillage raise and stabilise yields in dry years: compilers describe planting pits in Uganda keeping banana stands fruiting through drought and raising monthly harvests for sale, composting with planting pits in Burkina Faso raising farm income several times in dry years, and the Magoye ripper in Zambia improving yields and tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_959_2010_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income]. In the literature, returns to labour for these practices in Burkina Faso exceed the shadow wage, and bunds show positive returns at subproject level in Mauritania [ev_economic_return_kabo04_1, ev_economic_return_mrt14_5]. Compilers also judge benefits to outweigh establishment and maintenance costs in both the short and the long term on every sheet that rates them. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 USD per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots in the low-rainfall budget, with 866.84 against 357.16 for experienced farmers in high rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2], and ground cover raised the odds of a Malawian plot meeting the household maize requirement in the El Niño season, and planting basins sharply raised those odds in a good Kenyan season [ev_food_security_boil19_1, ev_food_security_boil19_2].
conditionality: Most units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, including the benefit-versus-cost judgements; the literature units are secondary model estimates for Burkina Faso and a lender self-reported subproject evaluation for Mauritania, and manual zai gives far smaller net benefits than mechanised zai in the same source [ev_economic_return_kabo04_1, ev_economic_return_mrt14_5, ev_economic_return_zoug14_1]. Several rated technologies bundle pits with compost or are conservation-tillage systems, and food security and farm income are proxies for poverty [ev_household_income_wocat_959_2010_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1139_2013_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Cost savings from conservation agriculture are usually small for smallholders, and in a Kenyan drought season net benefits were higher without tied ridging except with Tithonia [ev_economic_return_corb20_1, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]; the Zimbabwe margins include manure and fertiliser with the high-rainfall figure a sensitivity scenario, and the Kenyan planting-basin odds ratio has a wide confidence interval [ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_food_security_boil19_2].

effect_mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, farm ponds, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income and lean-season food security [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_household_income_ritc21_3, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6]. WOCAT compilers add that farm ponds in Cambodia keep enough irrigation water through drought, gully check dams in Ethiopia free rangeland for grazing, and gully rehabilitation in Somalia raised crop and livestock productivity [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Compilers' benefit-versus-cost ratings are positive or very positive over the long term for every sheet that rates them. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income and food security in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios of up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1].
conditionality: Most literature magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts, and practitioner ratings make up a large share of the pool [ev_household_income_saru19_3, ev_household_income_veno12_3]. Sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, Brazilian subsurface dams produced little cash income where electricity, investment capital or an irrigation tradition were missing, and the high Brazilian benefit-cost ratios come from an upper-middle-income context [ev_economic_return_ritc21_1, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7, ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. Compilers rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and an Indian subsistence farm pond as leaving farm income unchanged; Kenyan sand dams are embedded in a wider food-security programme [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Short-term returns on establishment are rated slightly to very negative on sheets from Tunisia, China, Nicaragua and Somalia, and the cost-benefit units are compiler judgements, not measured returns. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. The reviewed income, water-value and benefit-cost figures are secondary citations, reported at their upper end, and the Indian pond returns come from a cross-sectional preprint survey confounded by farm size and assets [ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1].

effect_mechanism: Terracing raises yields and enables higher-value crops on former hillsides, which drives positive modelled returns per hectare and improved food consumption in project households; terrace investments are judged to pay off over long lifetimes, mainly where they carry high-value crops such as vegetables [ev_economic_return_rwa18_8, ev_food_security_rwa18_5, ev_economic_return_willem21_1, ev_economic_return_fao13c_1]. WOCAT compilers report continuous income from tea on bench terraces in Thailand, a per-hectare income gain from progressive bench terraces in China, contour stone bunds in Bhutan meeting household maize demand, and Gradoni terraces in Uzbekistan improving drought resilience [ev_household_income_wocat_4281_2018_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1522_2010_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_6891_2023_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_7553_2025_risk_of_production_failure]. Compilers' benefit-versus-cost ratings are mostly positive or very positive over the long term. An Ethiopian synthesis reports positive net present values of 3486.2 Birr per hectare for stone bunds, 2794.0 for bench terraces and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3], and modelled bench-terrace gains in Peru could raise per capita incomes by up to 15% [ev_household_income_wei16_1].
conditionality: Most units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets; the literature returns are lender crop-budget models for Rwanda and India, and the food-security gain is an independent DIME evaluation [ev_economic_return_rwa18_8, ev_household_income_utk22_9, ev_food_security_rwa18_5]. A review reports terraces reducing net crop income in Ethiopia and banquette profitability in Niger was close to nil; compilers record no change in food security for vetiver terraces in Haiti, where farmers must wait for degraded soil to recover, and on sheets from Rwanda [ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_heusch95_1, ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Food security, income and returns are proxies for poverty. Compilers rate short-term returns on establishment as slightly negative to negative on sheets from Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde and Uzbekistan, and Rwanda's short-term maintenance return as very negative; these are practitioner judgements, not measured returns. The Ethiopian net present values are unweighted means from a few studies each, and the Peruvian income gain is a modelled potential cited in a review [ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_household_income_wei16_1].

effect_mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and lines, banquettes, trenches, pits and check dams slow overland flow and spread it behind barriers, so less runoff leaves the slope and less soil is detached and carried away; check dams and gabions trap sediment in channels. Measured reductions are large: terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, Burundi terrace plots cut erosion by 50% to 90%, trenches reduced soil loss by 73.0% on average, and check dams cut catchment sediment export by 20 to 98% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1]. WOCAT compilers across many countries rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced, explaining that micro-catchments cut the kinetic energy of rain by trapping runoff and that check dams slow runoff so soil accumulates upstream [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_soil_loss]. Meta-analyses confirm the direction: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil-loss reductions of 68.67% for mulching, 54.97% for ridging, 55.06% for soil and stone bunds and 60.21% for terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_2, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5]; an Ethiopian synthesis reports soil loss down 59% under graded soil bunds, 88% under level soil bunds, 38% under stone bunds, 98% under mulch and 62% under tied ridging [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_5]; and a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1]. At catchment scale, stone bunds, check dams and regrowth in Ethiopia cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year, and check dams on China's Loess Plateau reduced erosion rates from more than 200 to 20–25 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1].
conditionality: Over two thirds of the pool are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, and several literature sources are lender self-reports with before/after designs, perception surveys or catchment numbers that barely changed: the Rwanda sediment drop from 54 to 2.6 tons/ha a year has no control, and Indian sediment yield moved only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies. Negative findings: check dams can cause downstream channel incision, diversion banquettes increased gully and bank erosion in Niger, trenches raised sediment in the first years, Maghreb banquettes were often erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. Some sheets rate no change, including the Indian farm-pond sheet, and the Zambian tillage sheet expects less downstream siltation only if applied on a large scale [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation]. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. In the Ethiopian synthesis minimum tillage without residue raised soil loss by 14% and runoff by 19.4% [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_6, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_6]; in Tunisia gullied area on banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained banquettes in Algeria accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]; and USA check dams had no significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2]. The meta-analyses pool unweighted study means and are dominated by plot-scale East African studies, so catchment-scale effects remain less certain [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1].

effect_mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and lines and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1]. WOCAT compilers rate soil loss and runoff as reduced on terraces from China to Uzbekistan, noting that stone lines in Tunisia cut runoff by 50% and that Gradoni terraces trap soil eroded from the inter-spaces [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_6610_2022_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1522_2010_surface_runoff]. Meta-analyses agree: a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1], a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds terraces cut soil loss by 60.21% and runoff by 56.5%, and an Ethiopian synthesis reports stone bunds cutting soil loss by 38% and runoff by 34.4% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3]. Reviews also report terracing reducing runoff by 92.6% and 80% in sub-humid and humid regions, stone lines and terraces reducing runoff and erosion by 30 to 50%, sediment accumulating behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, and fanya juu trapping 64% of sediment, rising to 80% with vetiver grass [ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_2, ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6].

Bench terracing alone reduced runoff by only 9% in a small USA watershed, gullied area on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained Algerian banquettes accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on downstream dam sedimentation [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. effect_mechanism: Pits, bunds, terraces, trenches and check dams increase infiltration and groundwater recharge, raising well levels and spring discharge; sand dams and subsurface dams store water that extends the months of water access or backs up wells when other sources dry up, production cisterns keep livestock watered, and participating villages in India reduced water transport by tanker. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that more than 50% of runoff can infiltrate at check dams, with recharge tied to episodic storms, and that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1].
conditionality: Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix recharge, spring discharge and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger, and Ethiopian compilers note that off-site effects of recently built structures are yet to be assessed [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability]. Groundwater gains are often local and short-lived, can be wiped out by increased pumping, and year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season, and trenches had little effect on baseflow or infiltration [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. Upstream capture can reduce water downstream: streamflow on China's Loess Plateau fell by 39% after the check-dam campaign [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], mechanised bund systems in Morocco considerably reduce the water collected in downstream hill reservoirs and take 10 to 25% of the cultivable area [ev_water_yield_roos10_1], though a water-harvesting review notes downstream streamflow impacts of widely implemented small storage systems have in other cases been limited [ev_water_yield_rock10_1]. The new check-dam, pond and streamflow figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1].

effect_mechanism: Sand dams, check dams, subsurface dams, ponds and production cisterns store water in sand, soil or tanks and recharge local groundwater, extending the months of water access and keeping livestock watered when other sources dry up. WOCAT compilers for gabion check dams in Tunisia, check dam ponds and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia, sand dams in Kenya, stone check walls in India, on-farm ponds in Cambodia and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia judge them to improve water harvesting, quantity or availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1400_2011_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1547_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_harvesting_collection_of_water]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that more than 50% of runoff can infiltrate at check dams, with recharge tied to episodic storms, and that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1].
conditionality: The groundwater effect of sand dams is limited in space and time, many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season, and only part of assessed dams would hold enough water for reported beneficiaries [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. Several literature units are review citations or vote counts, the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and the Ethiopian compiler notes that off-site impacts of the recently built check dam still need assessment [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6716_2023_water_availability]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. Upstream capture can reduce water downstream: streamflow on China's Loess Plateau fell by 39% after the check-dam campaign [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. The check-dam and pond figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1].
